## Metrics v2 (REL-03; cost per FILLED share is primary, Perold shortfall secondary)

Pooled values are quantity-weighted ratios of sums (cluster-linearised CR1 SE, one cluster per session, Student-t at G − 1 df); ESS = parents / design effect; MDE = minimum detectable effect (80 % power, two-sided 5 %, Student-t). Narrower intervals are a diagnostic, never a gate.

Grid coverage: every cell ran on every session.

### Metric definitions

| metric | arrival price | target qty | horizon | benchmark | sign | unit | denominator |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cost_per_filled_share_bps` | mid at the parent window start (decision = arrival) | parent qty; only the FILLED quantity enters | fill time (no post-trade horizon) | arrival mid; trading cost + net fees + simulated impact adder | positive = worse (cost) | bps of the arrival mid | filled shares x arrival mid (sum over parents for the pooled ratio) |
| `trading_cost_per_filled_share_bps` | mid at the parent window start | filled qty only | fill time | Perold trading cost of the filled quantity (fill price vs arrival mid) | positive = worse | bps of the arrival mid | filled shares x arrival mid |
| `fill_rate` | n/a | parent qty | parent window | none (a diagnostic, not a target) | higher = more of the target traded | fraction | sum of parent target qty (qty-weighted); per-parent distribution beside it |
| `completion_ratio` | n/a | parent qty | parent window | none | higher = more parents finished | fraction of parents | number of parents (filled == target counts as complete) |
| `residual_qty` | n/a | parent qty | window end | target - filled | positive = unfilled | shares | none (sum; mean per parent beside it) |
| `completion_charge_bps` | mid at the parent window start | RESIDUAL qty only | window end | half-spread at the window end + taker fee, per residual share | positive = worse | bps of the arrival mid of the residual | residual shares x arrival mid |
| `shortfall_per_target_share_bps` | mid at the parent window start | parent qty | window end (opportunity cost marks the residual at the end mid) | Perold implementation shortfall = trading + opportunity (SECONDARY) | positive = worse | bps of the arrival notional of the TARGET | target qty x arrival mid |
| `arrival_markout_bps` | mid at the parent window start | filled qty | fill time | side-signed fill price minus arrival mid, quantity-weighted | positive = worse (paid above / sold below arrival) | bps of the arrival mid | filled shares x arrival mid |
| `post_trade_markout_bps` | n/a (relative to the fill price) | filled qty | per horizon h after each fill (1s, 5s, 30s) | side-signed (fill price - mid at fill + h), quantity-weighted | positive = worse (the price moved against the fill: adverse selection) | bps of the fill price | filled shares with a defined mid at +h (undefined fills are excluded, never zero) |

## Reading it

- `all_in = shortfall + fees_net + sim_impact + completion` per parent; the unfilled quantity is priced at the mid move and the cost of crossing at the window end, so not trading is never free.
- `sim_impact` is the configured adder (replay + linear child adder (rule 6)), not a measured reaction; the replayed book does not move for our fills.
- `depth-exhausted` (X-5): aggressive children cancelled because the walk ran out of displayed depth within the configured levels — the silent under-fill on thin names.
- provenance (X-7): which simulator rule produced the filled quantity (aggressive_walk, exec_print, marketable_add, hidden_print, cross, reopen_touch).
- Standard errors cluster by session; with few sessions the Student-t CI is wide by design and `low_power` is set in the JSON.
- urgency shares (B2 / B3): why each child of a signal-aware parent got its urgency (agree = posted on a favourable signal, adverse = crossed on an adverse one, neutral = inside the threshold, no_signal / stale = no usable reading, plain = a pacing-only arm).
- fades saved vs fills missed (B4 / B5): for every quantity a rule pulled, whether the market traded THROUGH the pulled price inside the horizon (the proxy for 'it would have filled') and the markout of that forgone fill — `saved` = it would have been adverse, `missed` = it would have been favourable; `lost race` = the fill landed before the cancel arrived (simulator rule 7). A counterfactual on a book our order never moved.
- markout by fill type (B6): passive = a first post that rested and filled, aggressive = a taker fill, faded = a maker fill that landed after a pull cancel was sent, cancelled_replaced = a maker fill of a child re-sent after a cancel; regimes are the B2 urgency regimes (plain without a signal). SEs cluster by session.
- dark (B10): fill type `dark` and every dark row above are MODELLED, NOT MEASURED — a logistic fill probability fitted on Nasdaq inside-spread hidden prints as the proxy (no dark-pool data exists); the negated price impact of the `dark` type is the adverse selection of those modelled fills.
